newsitem.title: USA: Novoste adopts shareholders right plan.
newsitem.headline: Novoste adopts shareholders right plan.

text.p: Novoste Corp said on Monday its board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan with a 15 percent trigger.

Under the plan, the company said shareholders of record on November 25 would receive one right for each outstanding share. Rights would be exercisable only after an entity acquired beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of Novoste common stock or began a tender offer resulting in that entity owning 15 percent or more of Novoste common stock, it said.

The plan was designed to encourage a potential suitor to negotiate with the company's board of directors before attempting a takeover, Novoste said. But it was not adopted in response to any specific takeover attempt, it said.
Novoste said rights would be respresented by existing common stock certificates until they became exercisable.

Each right would entitle the holder to buy a unit consisting of 1/100th of a share of a newly authorized series of Preferred Stock designated as Series A Participating Preferred stock, the company said.

After an entity acquired beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of the company's outstanding common stock, each right would then entitle its holder to buy, at an exercise price of $85, the number of shares of common stock having a market value of twice the right's exercise price.
Under certain circumstances, Novoste said it could redeem the rights at $0.01 each. They would expire on November 25, 2006 unless redeemed before that.
